title: How Much Does a Wedding Planner Cost in Punta Cana?
seoTitle: Wedding Planner Cost in Punta Cana: Fees and Inclusions
description: Compare wedding planner fees in Punta Cana: fixed prices, percentage models, inclusions, deposits and extra services to check before choosing your planner.
directAnswer: There is no single verified market-wide wedding planner fee for Punta Cana. The price depends on the service and the written agreement. As a specific published example, Sertuin Events lists standard full planning at USD 2,500 and wedding-day coordination at USD 1,200. These are planning fees, not complete wedding budgets. Compare responsibilities, event coverage, exclusions and payment terms before comparing the headline prices.

sections.heading: Start with the service you need, then compare the fee
paragraphs: If you are researching wedding planner cost in Punta Cana, first separate the price of professional planning from the cost of holding your celebration. A planning fee pays for an agreed scope of work: developing a plan, researching options, coordinating approved suppliers or managing the wedding day. A wedding budget also includes the services and products required to deliver that plan. A quote for planning alone cannot be compared directly with a resort package that includes a ceremony, food or accommodation.

Before requesting prices, write a short brief. Include the proposed date or date range, estimated guest count, preferred setting, number of events and decisions already made. Explain whether you need help selecting the venue, whether suppliers have been booked and who will manage communication from abroad. Mention any religious or cultural logistics without assuming that a planner can authorize a ceremony.

Then identify the work you want to hand over. A couple with a venue and signed supplier agreements may mainly need operational coordination. Another couple may want support from the first venue comparison through the reception. Both need a wedding professional, but they are buying different services. Giving each candidate the same brief makes the resulting proposals more useful and reduces the chance of discovering a service gap after paying a deposit.

sections.heading: Published Sertuin Events fees: a concrete reference
paragraphs: On the Sertuin Events service page consulted on November 18, 2026, standard full planning is listed at USD 2,500, wedding-day coordination at USD 1,200 and venue-and-vendor finding at USD 800. Specialized South Asian planning is listed at USD 4,999 for up to four event days; a fifth day is quoted separately. The published initial deposit for full and South Asian planning is USD 500.

These are this company's advertised fees, not a survey of Punta Cana prices. Standard full planning is described as a fixed fee regardless of guest count. The page states that third-party services are paid separately and that Sertuin does not receive commissions from recommended suppliers. Ask for a current written proposal confirming your precise scope, applicable taxes, payment schedule and any additional charges before contracting.

sources.label: Sertuin Events: planning services and published fees

sections.heading: Fixed fee, percentage or a combination: understand the calculation
paragraphs: A fixed fee assigns a stated price to defined work. Its usefulness depends on how clearly that work is described. Read the proposal for the number of event days, planning responsibilities and included attendance. Ask what happens if you later add a welcome dinner, another location or a second reception. A fixed fee for the original brief does not automatically cover every future change.

A percentage model calculates some or all compensation from a defined spending base. The important question is which expenses enter that base. Does it include only suppliers the planner manages, or also venue rental, accommodation, taxes and services you contracted independently? Ask whether there is a minimum fee and whether the final calculation uses the initial estimate or actual approved spending.

Consider an illustrative calculation, not a local rate recommendation: a hypothetical 10% fee on USD 30,000 of eligible expenses equals USD 3,000. If eligible spending rises to USD 40,000, the fee becomes USD 4,000. The example explains how a percentage works; it does not establish what a Punta Cana planner should charge.

Some agreements combine a fixed coordination fee with charges on particular purchases or additional services. One Dominican provider's published rates demonstrate such a mixed model, but that provider operates from the north coast and its terms should not be treated as a Punta Cana benchmark. The practical lesson is to request the complete calculation, including exclusions, rather than assume that one number describes every charge.

sources.label: Dominican Wedding Planner: an example of a mixed fee structure

sections.heading: What should a full-planning proposal explain?
paragraphs: Look for deliverables that you can recognize and review. For venue research, ask whether the planner provides a shortlist, compares proposals and helps arrange visits. For suppliers, ask who requests quotes, checks availability and tracks confirmations. For design, distinguish concept development from the physical production of flowers, furniture, lighting and installations. A design service can be included while production is billed separately.

Budget guidance also needs a practical definition. Ask whether you will receive an updated cost tracker, who records approved changes and how you will see pending payments. Make clear who can approve spending. A planner should know when an option is being considered and when it has actually been authorized; those are different stages.

Discuss communication in terms of real working arrangements: meetings, decision deadlines, the main contact and communication languages. If support is described as available around the clock, ask how urgent matters are routed and how ordinary planning questions are handled. For an international couple, knowing who will respond and how decisions are documented is more useful than a broad promise.

Finally, identify wedding-day responsibilities. Who coordinates arrivals, setup, the ceremony, photographs, the reception and the handover at the end? Are all venues covered? If activities happen simultaneously, how will the team cover them? These questions help assess the proposal without assuming a particular staffing level or promising that one person can be everywhere.

sections.heading: Day-of coordination: check the preparation as well as attendance
paragraphs: The phrase day-of coordination does not explain when preparation begins. Ask when the coordinator reviews your venue arrangements, supplier contacts and existing schedule. Find out what information you must deliver, what the coordinator will check and which problems remain your responsibility to resolve before the event. A successful handover requires more than giving someone a list of phone numbers on the wedding morning.

Coverage should be equally clear. Ask about arrival time, the end of attendance, setup supervision, guest movement and supplier communication. Confirm whether a rehearsal, welcome gathering or next-day brunch is included. Sertuin's published wedding-day service specifically excludes the rehearsal; another provider's proposal may define its scope differently.

Do not choose a smaller coordination service solely because its headline price is lower if you still need extensive planning. Make a list of unfinished decisions: venue, catering, décor, transport, accommodation arrangements and ceremony logistics. Ask the provider which of those tasks it will actually undertake. If several remain outside the package, account for the time or separate professional support needed to finish them.

A resort coordinator and an independent planner may also cover different responsibilities. Request a written division of work rather than assuming one replaces the other. Ask who handles hotel arrangements, external suppliers, events outside the property and communication with your guests. Any access conditions or outside-vendor charges must be confirmed with the specific resort.

sections.heading: Separate planning from supplier bills and travel expenses
paragraphs: Build two clearly labeled parts of your budget: professional planning and the celebration itself. In the second part, record venue hire, food and beverages, décor production, photography, video, entertainment, furniture, transport and accommodation as applicable. A planner may help source or coordinate these services without paying for them from the planning fee.

For each expense, record who signs the contract and who receives payment. If money passes through the planner, request a written explanation of what it covers and how supporting invoices will be provided. If you pay suppliers directly, clarify how payment confirmations reach the person coordinating the event. This is an organizational safeguard, not an assumption about any company's billing practices.

Ask separately about planner travel, accommodation, additional assistants, overtime and access to the venue. Do not assume that every provider charges these items or that none does. Your written proposal should either include them, exclude them or explain when they may apply. The same principle applies to taxes and transaction charges: ask for the final payable amount and currency instead of calculating an unverified universal surcharge.

If you budget in a currency other than USD, keep the contractual amount in its original currency and record a separate estimate in your home currency. Check conversion and transfer costs with your payment provider at the time of payment. Avoid treating an old exchange-rate conversion as the final cost of a deposit or balance.

sections.heading: Compare proposals using the same wedding brief
paragraphs: Create a comparison with the same questions for every candidate. Record the service scope, covered events, planning start date, on-site attendance, design responsibilities, supplier coordination, communication arrangements, exclusions and total quoted compensation. Mark missing answers as unresolved. A blank cell is a question to ask, not permission to assume that something is included.

Imagine two hypothetical proposals, one at USD 2,000 and another at USD 2,800. The first covers the wedding day only; the second also includes venue research and a separate welcome event. The difference is not simply USD 800 for identical work. Decide which tasks you need, obtain quotes for missing tasks and compare the resulting scope. These numbers are examples, not verified offers.

Evaluate independence and incentives with neutral questions. Does the planner receive supplier commissions, referral payments or markups? Are these disclosed? Can you choose a supplier outside the proposed list, subject to venue requirements? What happens if you already have a photographer or decorator? A transparent answer helps you understand the arrangement; price alone cannot answer those questions.

Do not assume that a planner will save more money than the fee. Any savings depend on the actual services selected and the alternatives available. Assess the value of the work you are delegating, the clarity of the process and the practicality of the proposed coverage. Ask for relevant examples or references, while respecting other clients' privacy.

sections.heading: Deposits, changes and cancellation questions to settle before booking
paragraphs: Ask for a payment schedule showing the amount, currency and due date of each instalment. Clarify whether an initial payment is credited toward the total fee and what action reserves the date. Avoid assuming that a deposit advertised for one service applies to another. Keep the signed scope, approved changes and payment confirmations together so both partners can consult the same record.

Read the arrangements for postponement, cancellation and changes in scope before paying. Ask what happens if the venue changes, the number of event days increases or the celebration is reduced. Request written terms for any additional work. This article does not interpret the legal effect of a contract; if a clause is unclear or significant to your decision, obtain an explanation from the provider and appropriate independent advice.

Discuss operational continuity as well. Who is your contact if the lead planner cannot attend, and how is the event information handed over? Ask how the team coordinates with the venue when a weather contingency is activated. A planning agreement should help you identify responsibilities, while the venue's own policies and supplier contracts may govern separate costs.

Do not rely on informal assurances that every change will be accommodated at no additional charge. Conversely, do not assume that every adjustment triggers a fee. Agree on a simple process: describe the requested change, obtain its effect on scope and price, and approve it in writing before new commitments are made.

sections.heading: Prepare a useful first conversation
paragraphs: Send a concise brief with your approximate guest count, possible dates, number of celebrations, venue preferences and available budget. Separate your overall wedding budget from any amount reserved for planning. Identify what has already been booked, what you want to decide yourselves and what support would make the greatest difference. This gives a planner a basis for proposing an appropriate service.

Bring your three main priorities and the compromises you are willing to consider. You might prioritize guest transport, a specific ceremony setting or help coordinating a multi-event schedule. Describe the need rather than demanding a package label. The planner can then explain the work involved, identify exclusions and propose a realistic handover.

Before choosing, make sure you can explain the proposal to each other in plain language: what you are buying, who will do it, which dates are covered, what remains to be purchased and when money is due. If you cannot answer one of those questions, request clarification. The right comparison starts with a shared understanding of the work, not the lowest number in a search result.
